rationale: C14 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both are Flag Day proclamations with closely corresponding recitals about the Continental Congress's adoption of the flag, refuge from oppression, and the flag as a symbol of freedom. More decisively, their operative provisions follow virtually the same sequence and repeatedly use matching language: directing display on all Government buildings, calling for suitable ceremonies and private display, and urging reflection on both privileges and responsibilities under the flag. C05 and C20 are also related annual templates, but neither matches the child's language and full operative structure as closely as C14.

shared_material.child_excerpt: people of many national origins and religious beliefs have found refuge from oppression and an opportunity for a better life under this beloved standard
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Americans of varied heritage, creed, and race have found refuge from oppression and surcease of fear under the protecting folds of Old Glory
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel recital combining diverse origins or creeds, refuge from oppression, and the protective national flag.

shared_material.child_excerpt: this flag is not only a symbol of freedom cherished by all Americans, but also an emblem of hope to millions of people dominated by ruthless dictatorships
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in our day the American flag symbolizes the realizes of the ideal of freedom in a world where that ideal is insecure
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the flag as a present international symbol of freedom threatened by oppression.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby direct that the flag be displayed on all Government buildings ... and I call upon the people of the Nation to observe that day by suitable ceremonies, including the display of the flag at their homes and other appropriate places
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings ... and I call upon the people of the Nation to observe that day as Flag Day by suitable ceremonies and by the display of the flag at their homes and other appropriate places
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim operative machinery and sequence, with only the date and minor wording adapted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: urge all our citizens to give special thought on Flag Day not only to their many rights and privileges but also to their duties and responsibilities under our national ensign
shared_material.parent_excerpt: urge all citizens to reflect upon the responsibilities which this banner enjoins as well as the privileges it carries
shared_material.explanation: Closely matched concluding exhortation pairing privileges under the flag with civic responsibilities.
